The author mentions the smart car is safe enough for the roads but I'm sure as hell not getting into one of those death traps either.

I'm not sure where I stand on this. I like less stupid laws but people are stupid and poor and will buy the cheapest shit that you offer. Whenever I drive past a wreck I'm happy to see destroyed cars but alive people.

The problem is the over-expansion of infrastructure without public transport system to support it. As a result more people need cars, but its too hard an unpopular for proper driver education, so we make cars idiot proof so when someone texting crashed into someone else, they have a higher chance of surviving.

So I can ride a motorcycle with no airbags and even no helmet in some jurisdictions but these cars are to unsafe. People should be able to decide what risk is acceptable for themselves and at what price.

The airbags are there to prevent you from coming into contact with windows and the steering wheel. Prior to airbags people were going partially through into (not always through) their windshields, bones broken when hitting the dashboard, and/or ejected from the car... even if you are wearing safety belts.

A motorcycle is another animal of vehicle. You sit ON it, not in it. It also weights less and carries less passengers. Basically if you ride a motorcycle, you are assuming a great deal of risk compared to riding in a car.

A $4,700 SUV? I'm totally calling bullshit.

There isn't a chance in hell anyone is going to be able to produce and sell such a vehicle in the US at a profit no matter what the regulations are. 3 billion people in the world live on under $2.50/day. You can't compare the price of goods and products in those markets to the United States.

Crying about regulations is absolutely nothing but lip service. You can barely buy a street legal motorcycle for that price in the US and it's 1/10th of the weight and requires none of the regulations or any of the ABS/TCS/airbags etc. you see in automobiles. Anyone who things they can cut back manufacturing costs for a product sold in the US is completely welcome to prove their case.

3 wheeled cars like like Aptera and Elio motors aren't required to meet the same safety requirements as 4 wheeled cars and every attempt at making a 3 wheeled car in the US has been met with complete and total failure. Elio is saying they can build one for $6,800 and so far all they have done is burn through hundreds of millions of dollars, delay the product launch, ask the government to fund their startup company with another 185 million or so with nothing but more delays expected on the roadmap.

They are not under the same regulation as other cars, nobody is stopping Elio from releasing the car they said they can release but Elio and it's looks like they will more likely scam a bunch of people out of their money than actually produce a real product.

As for safety I'm not ready to say the safety regulations are a bad either. Things like ABS, airbags, crumple zones etc. really do save a lot of peoples lives. I think there is room to make cars a bit smaller (and even maybe a 3 wheeled platform) but there is no way in hell anyone could make an SUV for $5k in the US no matter what the laws are.

Even if they were somehow successful the vehicle would be unrepairable disposable junk like Chineese scooters where you just scrap it after it stops working 6 months later.
I've been waiting for Elio to finally make something, but I don't believe all the hype the company makes. Three wheeled cars are motorcycles as far as the law is concerned.
